The first four sentences introduce the reasoning, the next four explain measurement discipline, and the final eight discuss safe delivery of a completed spoken answer. Equal unit groups provide simple experiment boundaries, avoiding a runtime sentence classifier and ensuring every candidate request covers one contiguous portion of the same final text. That design makes audits direct: reviewers join the request strings, compare them with the final, and confirm that no overlap, omission, or reorder entered the result. Parallel requests can begin useful work sooner, but their audio remains behind an ordered release frontier so a later phrase never reaches presentation before the words that introduce it. When the first chunk supplies valid samples, its timing is the only credited first-source measure; an earlier successor sample is diagnostic, not playable speech. If any request fails, times out, or is cancelled, the group fence stops live streams, discards unreleased samples, and records failure instead of pretending that a partial answer completed. A bounded scheduler permits two active requests, then replenishes a four-chunk group only after the ordered frontier moves, limiting concurrency without sacrificing the comparison shape.
